item.title: How a Cornell Student Went From Shame to Anger
item.description: The woman known as “Jane Doe” was initially embarrassed about what happened at a fraternity party in 2024, but soon concluded: “I was assaulted.”
item.dc:creator: Debra Kamin, Matt Flegenheimer, Amy Julia Harris and Sharon Otterman
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Prosecutors have reopened the case of a woman who said she was sexually assaulted by Cornell University fraternity brothers in 2024.

item.title: The Cornell Rape Investigation: Five Takeaways
item.description: The New York Times obtained more than 1,000 pages from the university’s internal inquiry into accusations by “Jane Doe.” Here are the revelations so far.
item.dc:creator: Sharon Otterman
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: Cornell University’s investigation of a 2024 sexual assault allegation included interviews, emails and screenshots.

item.title: Statement Written by Police in Cornell Assault Case Omitted Her Claim She Was Raped
item.description: Documents obtained by The New York Times show that the campus police at Cornell University sent a condensed statement to a prosecutor, who then declined to bring charges.
item.dc:creator: Hurubie Meko
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Cornell Police Department summarized hours of interviews with a woman who said she was raped into a six-page document that excluded key details. A local prosecutor did not pursue criminal charges based on that document.

item.title: What Newly Obtained Documents Show About the Cornell Case, and Inside the Bloody Midair Cockpit Attack
item.description: Plus, a Kelvin wave is coming.
item.dc:creator: Tracy Mumford, Will Jarvis, Margaret Kadifa, Jake Lucas, Ian Stewart and Emma Goldberg
item.media:credit: Heather Ainsworth for The New York Times

item.title: After Failed Attempt to Execute Christa Pike, Tennessee Pauses a Planned Execution
item.description: Gov. Bill Lee, a Republican, ordered a review of the state’s lethal injection process after the botched attempt to put Christa Pike to death. She was hospitalized Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Emily Cochrane
item.media:credit: George Walker Iv/Associated Press
item.media:description: Governor Bill Lee delivers his State of the State address earlier this year. Lee has ordered a review of the execution process following the botched execution of Christa Pike on Wednesday.

item.title: What to Know About the Attempted Execution of Christa Pike
item.description: Ms. Pike, 50, survived two doses of lethal injection in Tennessee. She was sentenced to death for the 1995 murder of a classmate.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang
item.media:credit: George Walker Iv/Associated Press
item.media:description: Media witnesses recounted the moments before the execution of Christa Pike was halted on Wednesday.

item.media:description: Gina Hinojosa is the Democratic candidate running for governor of Texas against the incumbent, Gov. Greg Abbott.

item.title: Who Is Captain Smit Machchhar, the Pilot Hailed as a Hero After FlyDubai Cockpit Stabbing?
item.description: Capt. Smit Machchhar suffered stab wounds while fending off an attack from his co-pilot, saving the lives of around 170 people on board, officials said.
item.dc:creator: Somini Sengupta, Suhasini Raj and Mujib Mashal
item.media:credit: Israel Foreign Ministry, via Reuters
item.media:description: A photograph provided by the Israeli government shows Smit Machchhar, an Indian pilot, in an undated handout image released on Wednesday.

item.title: A Bloody Attack on a FlyDubai Plane Headed to Israel, and a Terrifying Plunge
item.description: “I don’t deserve to die like this,” said one passenger on Flight 1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv. The motive of the cockpit stabbing remains unknown, officials said.

item.title: Taking On Trump Immigration Agenda, Justices Will Review Migrant Detention Policy
item.description: The administration’s policy of detaining immigrants who crossed the border illegally years ago and holding them without a bond hearing has divided lower courts.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: The Supreme Court will be considering the legality of some of the most controversial aspects of the Trump administration’s efforts to rapidly expel millions of migrants living in the United States.

item.title: John Roberts Retreated to His Island. Supreme Court Critics Found Him.
